author: c. w. singer
title: Lightning defeat Sharks as point streak reaches 14 games - San Jose Standard
text:
Brandon Hagel scored twice and had an assist as the Tampa Bay Lightning defeated the San Jose Sharks 4-1 at Benchmark International Arena on Tuesday, extending their point streak to 14 games. The Lightning, now 31-13-4, are 13-0-1 during this run.
Jake Guentzel and Anthony Cirelli each contributed a goal and an assist for Tampa Bay. Nikita Kucherov added three assists, while goaltender Andrei Vasilevskiy made 22 saves.
“These are always dicey games, especially when you go on a five-game [road trip] and you come back and you just don’t want to take a breath,” said Lightning coach Jon Cooper. “The guys didn’t take a breath tonight. You need this [streak] just to stay relevant in the Atlantic. You kind of need to go on these to make sure you’re putting yourself in a spot to make the playoffs.”
For San Jose (25-21-3), Tyler Toffoli scored the team’s only goal after they were coming off a win against the Florida Panthers the previous night. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 16 shots for the Sharks.
“We didn’t win enough pucks in all three zones, especially the offensive zone,” said Sharks coach Ryan Warsofsky. “We did some good things in that first period. We had a good road period, but we handed them one there at the end of the first. The second we weren’t great and the third we kind of ran out of gas.”
Toffoli opened scoring for San Jose late in the first period with help from William Eklund and Alexander Wennberg. “[Eklund] did a good job breaking away and getting a little space for himself, and I just went to the net and it was just a fortunate bounce,” Toffoli said. “I think we found a way to generate some more opportunities, but that’s also a very good goalie in there.”
Hagel quickly tied it less than a minute later after Kucherov forced a turnover leading to Cirelli setting up Hagel at close range.
“When everyone is buying into their role and their job every time they step on the ice, it makes it easy for the goals to go into the net,” Hagel said. “Especially when you’re playing good defense and you’ve got ‘Vasy’ kicking. There’s so many saves he makes that give us confidence.”
Cirelli gave Tampa Bay its first lead early in the second period before leaving with an undisclosed injury early in the third; no update was provided postgame by Cooper.
Guentzel extended Tampa’s lead later in that period following assists from Gage Goncalves and Dominic James.
“It’s obviously fun when you’re winning. It’s a lot easier when you’re winning and it’s a lot more fun,” James said. “It’s fun playing with two guys that can make such great plays. If you get it to them they’re going to score, like Jake did tonight.”
Hagel sealed victory with an empty-net goal late in regulation.
“I think it was just tough to get stuff going offensively,” Sharks rookie center Michael Misa said. “We didn’t have much going on. We had some chances, but we just couldn’t score.”
Sharks forward Macklin Celebrini failed to record points in consecutive games for only his second time this season while Hagel has tallied 15 points over his last ten appearances.
